messages:
Zoe Kim: Hey everyone  day 2 question: where should I post different onboarding problems? VPN, laptop delivery, GitHub access. Also curious which bots are fine to poke vs which I should avoid.
Ravi Desai: welcome Zoe! super short map: hardware/HR -> #people-ops (use the pinned ordering form), access/VPN -> #eng-infra for requests and #help if it's blocking you right now, GitHub/org invites -> open the SSO ticket from #help and include your GH username.
Marta Lopez: if something is blocking you from doing work (no VPN, can't clone) post in #help and mention @eng-oncall. That channel gets oncall attention during working hours.
Zoe Kim: cool. about bots  there's a "reaction-games" bot in #random and a deploy app in #eng-releases. can I try them?
Ravi Desai: rule of thumb: if the app/bot is marked "sandbox" or "test" in its description, it's safe in public. otherwise, test it in #dev-bots or DM the bot. never run deploy/pipeline slash commands in public unless you know the flow.
Onboarding Bot: Hi Zoe! To re-run your onboarding checklist use `/onboard me` and I will DM you steps. Use `/onboard status` to see what's left.
Zoe Kim: thanks! any quick posting etiquette so I don't clog channels?
Marta Lopez: TL;DR: 1) Search handbook + Slack history first. 2) Post in the most specific channel (avoid #general). 3) Use threads for follow-ups. 4) Include what you tried and minimal logs in fenced code blocks. 5) Don't paste secrets; use the secret manager or DM.
Ravi Desai: Example for an error post (good): "@eng build failing on ubuntu-22, ran `make build`, last 6 lines below" then a fenced block with the 6 relevant lines. For long traces, put an unlisted gist and link it.
Zoe Kim: if I accidentally post a credential, what's the exact flow?
Marta Lopez: delete the message immediately, rotate the credential, then ping #eng-security. There's a secrets-runbook pinned in #eng-security with step-by-step.
IT Ticket Bot: For hardware/shipping tickets, open https://peopleops.internal/tickets and include your manager and shipping address. Mark "priority" if it's urgent.
Ravi Desai: one more: if you want to safely experiment with slash commands (deploy, ci, polls), use #dev-bots or a DM with the bot. We keep some channels read-only (monitoring/deploy feeds)  check the channel header before posting.
Zoe Kim: awesome, super clear. I'll use #help for blockers and #dev-bots for testing. Thanks y'all :raised_hands:
